meaning.name: The nightly run
meaning.purpose: The timer starts the job; by the morning the shop's stock matches the supplier's feed, or the operator on call has a mail that says why it does not.
meaning.steps: 1. At 02:30 Berlin time, or up to five minutes after, the timer starts a run; a night missed while the host was down runs when it is up again. A1, R1 2. The run takes the lock; where another run holds one younger than six hours, it ends held off, says so in the log and mails the morning. A1, R7, R6 3. The run fetches the feed, and where the supplier answers 503 or nothing, tries again ten minutes later, three tries in all. A1, R2 4. The run checks the feed: its rows, its three columns, its quantities, and that it was made within 36 hours; a feed that fails is refused and nothing is written. A1, R3 5. The run compares the feed with the shop's stock, SKU by SKU, passing over what the shop does not sell; where nothing differs it ends with nothing to do, and where more than half would change it is refused. A1, R5, R4 6. The run writes each change to the catalogue; where the catalogue refuses one, it stops, and what was written stays. A1, R5 7. The run keeps the report, mails it where any SKU is low, out of stock or no longer in the feed, writes its last line to the log, and gives the lock back. A1, R6, R10, R11 8. At 08:00 the operator on call reads the mail; a night without one went as it should.
meaning.trigger: the timer, every night at 02:30, Berlin time

meaning.goes wrong: | What fails | Then | Seen by | Stands on | |---|---|---|---| | the supplier still answers 503 after 08:00 | the rerun is refused with exit 2, R2 | the operator, on the command's exit code and in the log; the supplier's desk is called | R2 | | the catalogue still refuses the same SKU | the rerun stops with exit 3, the writes before it kept, R5 | the operator, by the exit code and the mail naming the SKU | R5 | | the operator removes a lock while a run is still going | two runs write at once, which the lock is there to prevent, R7 | nobody, until two lines of the log disagree: the runbook says to look for the process first | R7 | | a feed file the operator gives is stale or out of shape | refused as the fetched feed would be, R9 | the operator, on the exit code and the reason | R9 |
meaning.name: A rerun by hand
meaning.purpose: The operator on call, with a mail that says the night failed, ends with the shop's stock in line with the feed, or with the supplier called.
meaning.steps: 1. The operator reads the morning mail, which says FAILED and why, and opens the runbook at that outcome. R6 2. Where the feed could not be fetched, the supplier's rebuild ran late: the operator waits until after 08:00 and runs the job by hand. A1, R2 3. Where the feed was stale, the operator calls the supplier's desk and does not rerun with the old feed; a feed file of the old one would be refused all the same. A3, R9, R3 4. Where the feed was out of shape, the operator keeps the feed as a file for the developer; nothing is written until the job reads the new form. A3, R9 5. Where a write was refused, the operator waits for the catalogue and runs the job by hand; the rerun writes only what still differs. A1, R5 6. Where the run was held off and no run is going, the operator removes the lock left behind and runs the job by hand. A1, R7 7. The rerun ends done or with nothing to do, and its outcome is in the day's log; where the supplier still answers 503, the operator calls its desk. A1, R10 8. The operator calls the supplier's desk by phone, outside the job.

meaning.name: Report

meaning.question: Can the catalogue take a night's changes as one write, all or none, so that a refused write leaves nothing half done (R5)?
meaning.why: today a refused write leaves the SKUs before it written and those after it not, and the rerun mends it; one write would make the rerun needless

meaning.name: Run every night
meaning.statement: When it is 02:30 in Berlin, the stock sync shall start one run that brings the shop's stock in line with the supplier's feed.

meaning.says: Given the host is up, when the clock in Berlin reaches 02:30, then a run starts by 02:35 and its first line is in the night's log.
Given the host was down from 02:00 to 06:10, when it is up again, then the run of that night starts and the night is not lost.
Given a run still going 45 minutes after its start, when the 45th minute passes, then it is stopped, and the morning hears of it as a run that stopped, R6.
Given the summer's time and the winter's, when the night comes, then the run starts at 02:30 by the clock in Berlin in both.

meaning.name: The night's log, step by step
meaning.statement: The stock sync shall write a line to the day's log for each step of a run: its start, each try of the feed that failed, the feed fetched with its rows and the time it was made, each SKU listed again, the SKUs not sold, the SKUs that differ, those written, the report and the mail, and how the run ended.

meaning.says: Given the night of 10 October, when the run ends, then the log holds, in order: "starting: feed" and its address, "feed answered 503 on try 1", "fetched 1,214 rows, as of 2026-10-10 00:58 UTC", "line 388: AC-VLT-65 listed again; the last row wins", "41 SKU(s) of the feed are not sold by the shop", "23 SKU(s) differ from the shop's stock", "written: 23 SKU(s)", "report written" with its place, the low and the out and the mail, and "done: 23 SKU(s) changed".
Given a run refused or stopped, when it ends, then its last line says why, as the mail does.
Given two runs on one day, when both end, then both are in that day's log, one after the other.

meaning.name: Name the SKUs the feed no longer carries
meaning.statement: When a run ends, the stock sync shall list in the night's report every SKU the shop sells that the feed does not carry, with the shop's quantity of each, and leave that quantity as it is.

meaning.says: Given the shop sells LT-ZEN-12 at 6 and the feed no longer carries it, when the run ends, then the report lists "LT-ZEN-12: 6, not in the feed", and its quantity stays 6.
Given 12 such SKUs and nothing else to report, when the run ends, then the mail comes with the 12, R6.
Given every SKU of the shop is in the feed, when the run ends, then the report says "none" under that heading.

meaning.name: A second supplier
meaning.statement: When a second supplier's feed is given, the stock sync shall bring the shop's stock in line with both.

meaning.name: Fetch the feed, three times at most
meaning.statement: When a run starts, the stock sync shall fetch the supplier's feed, and where the supplier does not answer with it, try again up to two more times, ten minutes apart.

meaning.says: Given the supplier answers 503 at 02:31 and the feed at 02:41, when the run fetches it, then the log shows the 503 on the first try and the feed fetched on the second, and the run goes on.
Given the supplier answers nothing within 30 seconds, when the run fetches, then that try counts as failed and the next comes ten minutes later.
Given three tries fail, when the third has failed, then the run is refused with "the feed could not be fetched in 3 tries", the shop's stock is as it was, and the morning is mailed, R6.

meaning.name: Refuse a feed that cannot be right
meaning.statement: If the feed has no rows, lacks its SKU, its quantity or the time it was made, holds a quantity that is not a whole number of none or more, or was made more than 36 hours before the run, then the stock sync shall refuse the run, change nothing, and say why.

meaning.says: Given a feed of the header alone, when it is read, then the run is refused with "the feed has no rows" and ends with exit 2.
Given a feed that does not say when it was made, when it is read, then the run is refused, and the reason names as_of.
Given a quantity of "forty" on line 12, when it is read, then the run is refused with "line 12: quantity 'forty' is not a whole number".
Given a quantity of -2 on line 7, when it is read, then the run is refused with "line 7: quantity -2 is below zero".
Given a feed made 37 hours before the run, when it is read, then the run is refused with the time it was made and "older than 36 hours"; one made 35 hours before is read.
Given any of these refusals, when the run ends, then no SKU of the shop has changed and the morning is mailed with the reason, R6.

meaning.name: Refuse a change too large to be real
meaning.statement: If more than half of the shop's SKUs would change at once, then the stock sync shall refuse the run and change nothing.

meaning.says: Given a shop of 1,000 SKUs and a feed that changes 501 of them, when the two are compared, then the run is refused with "501 of 1000 SKUs would change: more than 50%", ends with exit 2, and no SKU changes.
Given a feed that changes 500 of the 1,000, when the two are compared, then the run goes on and writes the 500.
Given the guard refused a feed, when the morning comes, then the mail says how many would have changed of how many, R6.

meaning.name: Bring the shop's stock in line with the feed
meaning.statement: When the feed is read and passes its checks, the stock sync shall set each SKU the shop sells whose quantity differs from the feed's to the feed's quantity, and leave every other SKU as it is.

meaning.says: Given the shop holds A at 1 and B at 5, and the feed says A 1 and B 2, when the run writes, then B is 2, A is untouched, and the run ends with "done: 1 SKU(s) changed" and exit 0.
Given a SKU of the feed the shop does not sell, when the two are compared, then it is passed over, and the log counts it.
Given a SKU the shop sells that the feed does not carry, when the two are compared, then its quantity stays the shop's own, R11.
Given a SKU listed twice, at 40 and then 38, when the feed is read, then 38 is the feed's quantity and the log names the line of the second.
Given nothing differs, when the two are compared, then nothing is written and the run ends with "nothing to do" and exit 1.
Given the catalogue refuses the write of the 9th of 23 SKUs, when it refuses, then the run stops with exit 3 naming that SKU, the 8 before it stay written, and the 14 after it are not written.
Given a run stopped so, when the operator reruns it, then only what still differs is written.

meaning.name: Tell the morning
meaning.statement: When a run ends with any SKU low, out of stock or no longer in the feed, or without doing its work for any reason, the stock sync shall mail the operations team the night's report or the reason it stopped.

meaning.says: Given a run that wrote 23 SKUs, 4 of them now at 3 or fewer and 2 at none, when it ends, then the report is kept for the day and mailed with the subject "Stock sync 2026-10-10: low stock": the time in UTC and the outcome, "23 SKU(s) changed", the 4 low and the 2 out by SKU, and each change as "SKU: before → after".
Given a night with nothing to do and one SKU at 2, when the run ends, then the mail comes all the same, with that SKU among the low.
Given a night with nothing to do, no SKU at 3 or fewer and every SKU of the shop in the feed, when the run ends, then no mail comes, and the log says nothing changed.
Given the feed refused or a write refused, when the run ends, then the mail's subject says FAILED and why, and its body says the reason and to see the runbook.
Given the catalogue does not answer with the shop's stock, or any other stop the runbook does not name, when the run ends, then the mail's subject says FAILED, and the run ends with exit 5.
Given a run held off by another's lock, when it ends, then the mail says so, R7.

meaning.name: One run at a time
meaning.statement: While a run is going, the stock sync shall hold any other run off, and take over a lock left behind for more than six hours.

meaning.says: Given a run that started at 02:31 and is still going, when another is started by hand at 02:40, then the second writes nothing, says "another run holds the lock" with where the lock is, and ends with exit 4.
Given a run that ended, whatever its outcome, when the next starts, then the lock is free.
Given a lock left by a run that died 7 hours before, when the next run starts, then it takes the lock over and runs.
Given a lock left 5 hours before and no run going, when the next run starts, then it is held off, and the operator removes the lock as the runbook says.

meaning.name: A dry run
meaning.statement: When the operator asks for a dry run, the stock sync shall read the feed, compare it with the shop's stock and print the report of what would change, and write nothing to the catalogue and mail nothing.

meaning.says: Given a feed that changes 23 SKUs, when the operator runs a dry run, then the report is printed with "dry run, nothing written" and the 23 changes, the catalogue is unchanged, and the run ends with exit 0.
Given a stock take that changes 640 of 1,000 SKUs, when the operator runs a dry run, then the report of the 640 is printed with a line that says the guard would refuse it, R4.
Given a feed refused for its shape or its age, when the operator runs a dry run, then the reason is printed and no mail is sent.

meaning.name: A rerun from a feed file
meaning.statement: When the operator gives a feed file, the stock sync shall read it in place of the supplier's address and hold it to every check the fetched feed is held to.

meaning.says: Given a feed file saved from the supplier this morning, when the operator runs with it, then the run reads it, nothing is fetched, and it goes on as a night's run.
Given a feed file made two days before, when the operator runs with it, then the run is refused as stale, as the fetched feed would be.
Given a file that does not exist, when the operator runs with it, then the run stops, says so, and ends with exit 5.

The runbook sends the operator to a dry run to read the report before a stock take; the job's guard refuses before any report is made, in a dry run too

The log of 10 October holds a line for each step -- starting, fetched, differ, written, report written; the job read writes only the last of them

meaning.name: security

meaning.name: proof
meaning.says: Each night's report and log are kept for at least 31 days, so that the operator can look back a month (E12).

meaning.assumptions: - The supplier rebuilds the feed by 01:00 Berlin time, and a run at 02:30 finds it made within the last few hours. To check: the time each night's feed was made, in a month of logs. - The operations team counts the orders cancelled for missing stock the same way after the move. To check: ask for the count of the first month after launch.
meaning.journey: 1. At 01:00 the supplier rebuilds the feed; at 02:30 the timer starts the job. 2. The job fetches the feed, trying again ten minutes later while the supplier answers that it is still rebuilding. 3. It checks the feed, compares it with the shop's stock SKU by SKU, and refuses the whole run where the change is too large to be real. 4. It writes each new quantity to the catalogue, writes the night's report, and mails the operator where anything is low. 5. At 08:00 the operator reads the mail, or its absence; today a run that stopped on the catalogue's side sends nothing, and the night goes unnoticed until a customer phones. 6. Where the night went wrong, the operator follows the runbook: waits, reruns by hand, removes a lock left behind, or calls the supplier.
meaning.name: Stock sync
meaning.non-goals: - A second supplier: the job reads one feed, Nordkabel's, and the brief puts any other on the list for later (E5). - Ordering from the supplier when stock runs low, and taking prices from the feed: the job sets quantities and nothing else (E5). - Setting the stock of a product the feed no longer lists: the job names it, and the catalogue team sets it (E10, R11). - Pages or an interface of its own: the job is read through its mail, its report, its log and its exit code (E73).
meaning.problem: The job's author has left, and the job moves to a new platform; without a specification the new team would read the old code and guess (E1). In September 2026, 31 orders were cancelled because the product was not there to ship, about seven a week; most were products the supplier had stopped listing, which the shop went on showing in stock (E2, E24). Three nights in September the run failed and nobody knew until a customer phoned, and each such morning cost the operator on call about three hours (E3, E31).
meaning.summary: The stock sync is Voltline's nightly job that takes the supplier's stock feed, refuses a feed that cannot be right, brings the shop's stock in line with it, and tells the operator on call in the morning what changed and what is running low. No user drives it: a timer starts it at 02:30, and the operator runs it by hand from the runbook when a night went wrong. This specification says what it does today, so that the team moving it to the new platform with the shop in the spring of 2027 builds the same job, less the holes the operations lead names (E1).
meaning.users: The timer: the scheduler that starts one run every night at 02:30, Berlin time (U1). The operator on call: one of the three people in operations, a week each in turn, who reads the morning mail and, when a night went wrong, follows the runbook and runs the job by hand (U2). The supplier, Nordkabel, who rebuilds the stock feed at 01:00 every night and publishes it at one address (U3). The catalogue: the shop's own store of products and their stock, which the shop's pages read and the job writes to (U4). The catalogue team sets by hand the stock of what the supplier does not list (E4).
